Topic 4.1: Observing and articulating signs(Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Proper articulation of signs and vocabulary
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Observing and articulating signs(Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Proper articulation of signs and vocabulary, part of ROAD ACCIDENTS - PREVENTION Suggested Vocabulary to be signed skid, speed, hit a in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade five General.

Key inquiry question: Why should we pronounce or observe the proper place of articulation of signs and fingerspelling words correctly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Observing and articulating signs(Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Proper articulation of signs and vocabulary together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: articulating signs clearly as learner practises correct pronunciation or observing proper place of articulation

of signs and fingerspelling words in small groups.

• Self-Efficacy: the learner recites by signing poems and stress words and signing in context; words spelt same while varying facial expression

and body movement correctly

Values:
Love: Selflessness as learners help one another to improve their pronunciation or observing proper place of articulation of signs and fingerspelling

with the correct mouth movement

Link to other Subjects:

Studies.
